hypothesis: Withdrawing and identically reposting an unbooked gig may renew notifications and improve booking without raising the fee. Reposted cars retain their original age.
scope: Bounded ordinary-practice mechanism probe on an old development seed; no ranking.
selection: First eligible unsampled order in snapshot, checked at most once every30 simulated minutes from08:00 through18:00. Open single-car public gig aged at least30min; waiting order, pickup ready within180min and lastPickupAt at least180min away.
measurement: Target-gig views, unique viewers and bookings through10 and30min. Compare hold with unchanged reprice as a sham. Base policy continues unchanged between samples and through full week; compare complete events and score with archived control.
decision: No full-policy implementation unless relisting adds bookings or useful views in this bounded screen. A positive mechanism is not full-week profit evidence and must justify a separate frozen policy experiment. Retain every case and failure; do not extend the sample after seeing outcomes.
limitations: Relisting changes gig identity and history as well as possible notifications; a positive result does not uniquely identify notifications.
One old stream, first12 eligible cases, selected unbooked jobs; not representative profit evidence.
Forks receive no other dispatcher actions for30min in every arm.
failureRule: Stop on any refused or uncertain fork mutation. Attempt deletion of all known temporary forks; retain base and report on failure. No automatic retries or replacement cases.
